probes.question: In the Bakhshali manuscript, zero is shown as a ____ used as a placeholder.
What does shunya-bindu literally mean?
options: The dot of the empty place

image.alt: Flat illustration of a sandstone slab carved with a row of five tally marks ending in one small round circle, under a warm sun.

panels.text: In 1881, a peasant dug up an old manuscript in a field near the village of Bakhshali, in present-day Pakistan.
It is written on birch bark: seventy fragile leaves of arithmetic problems in Sanskrit.
The numbers use place value, and where we would write a zero, it uses a simple dot as a placeholder. That dot was called the shunya-bindu: literally, the dot of the empty place.
Until 2024 it was regarded as the earliest known Indian use of a zero symbol. New carbon dating by Oxford places the manuscript between 799 and 1102 CE, so the story keeps being rewritten.
